title: A Phone Call About Mercy After Ta’if
script: Amir: [thoughtful] Laila, I read a report about the Prophet Muhammad after his difficult visit to Ta’if.
Laila: What happened during that visit?
Amir: He invited the people to worship Allah, but they rejected him and treated him cruelly.
Laila: [sadly] He must have felt deep pain after leaving the city.
Amir: Yes. Later, the angel of the mountains came with an offer to crush the people between two mountains.
Laila: That was a moment when punishment was possible. How did the Prophet respond?
Amir: [gently] He did not ask for their destruction. He hoped that their descendants would worship Allah alone.
Laila: He hoped for good from families whose people had just harmed him?
Amir: Exactly. His mercy looked beyond his own pain and beyond that one terrible day.
Laila: [reflective] Mercy is much harder when a person has the power to answer harm with harm.
Amir: That is why this account stayed with me. He did not call cruelty good, but he still wanted guidance for them.
Laila: So forgiveness does not mean saying that the wrong action was acceptable.
Amir: [carefully] Right. We can name a wrong, protect people from harm, and still avoid personal revenge.
Laila: How can we use that lesson in an ordinary disagreement?
Amir: We can pause before answering, choose fair words, and ask Allah to guide everyone involved.
Laila: [honestly] I often prepare a sharp reply before I think about what it may cause.
Amir: I do too. The story gives us a higher example, even if our own problems are much smaller.
Laila: It also reminds me that another person may change later.
Amir: [hopeful] Yes. We should not close the door to guidance because of one painful moment.
Laila: Thank you for calling. This is a clear lesson in mercy, truth, and self-control.

quiz.explanation: The Prophet hoped for faith among later generations.

quiz.question: What does Laila learn about forgiveness?

quiz.explanation: Truth and mercy can exist together.

quiz.explanation: The conversation looks beyond one bad moment.
